note: Every external input of the build and the hosted workflow: version, source, SHA-256 and license. Read by cmake/CrdPins.cmake, scripts/pins.py and scripts/check-pins.py; contract in docs/design/pinned-inputs.md. Refresh an entry by editing it here only.

aws-lc.note: AWS-LC 5.12.0 (released 2026-10-23), crd-crypto's provider (NET.2): libcrypto only, linked privately into crd-crypto, assembled from its pregenerated sources (no Perl, no Go). LICENSE read from the archive: AWS-LC's own code Apache-2.0 OR ISC, BoringSSL- and OpenSSL-derived code ISC and Apache-2.0, mlkem-native and mldsa-native Apache-2.0 OR ISC OR MIT, fiat-crypto MIT, s2n-bignum Apache-2.0 OR ISC OR MIT-0, jitterentropy BSD-3-Clause (dual-licensed with GPL-2.0, taken under BSD-3-Clause). openssl.gated: CRD_BUILD_TLS_VS_OPENSSL or CRD_BUILD_MLS_VS_MLSPP or CRD_BUILD_CRYPTO_VS_PEERS or CRD_BUILD_QUIC_VS_NGTCP2
openssl.provenance: the GitHub release openssl/openssl openssl-4.0.3, where https://www.openssl.org/source/ now redirects (the same SHA-256 as openssl.org's openssl-4.0.3.tar.gz.sha256 and the openssl-4.0.3.tar.gz.sha256 of that release, read 2026-11-02; the direct URL since 2026-11-09, when a redirect loop through openssl.org failed a cold download)
openssl.note: OpenSSL 4.0.3 (released 2026-09-29, a security release of the 4.0 series, which added Encrypted Client Hello, RFC 9849, beside 3.5's ML-KEM and hybrid TLS groups and its QUIC TLS interface), the independent TLS 1.3 and ECH peer of crd-crypto's sessions (NET.2); it replaced 3.5.9, which has no ECH, on 2026-11-02. Built by its own Perl Configure as a separate project, static, libraries only, linked only into crd-openssl-tls-peer for the crd-crypto-tls-interop-openssl CTest, into crd-mlspp-peer (MLSpp's crypto) for the crd-crypto-mls-interop-mlspp CTest and into crd-crypto-board for the crypto boards; never into an engine module or a default build. LICENSE.txt read from the archive: Apache-2.0. Pinned as a testing download under the user's approval of 2026-11-01 (docs/sessions/2026-11-02-net-2-ech.md).

boringssl.provenance: https://github.com/google/boringssl/releases/tag/0.20261020.0 (the tag names commit d3bf4795; this commit archive unpacks to the same files as the release's own source archive boringssl-0.20261020.0.tar.gz, whose SHA-256 fb43aac7fbd323c9dfa1f45fe92a1c01142433c05b23fe34f61d6ba8b13b642e matches the digest GitHub publishes for the asset, compared file by file on 2026-11-03)
boringssl.note: BoringSSL 0.20261020.0 (released 2026-10-20, the newest of its dated releases), the second peer library of crd-crypto's boards (NET.2: AEAD, X25519, ML-KEM-768, Ed25519, ECDSA P-256 and ML-DSA-65 rates and TLS 1.3 handshakes and record throughput, docs/bench). Built by its own CMake as a separate project from its pregenerated sources (no Go, no Perl), static, crypto and ssl only, with its symbols prefixed crd_bssl (BORINGSSL_PREFIX, its checked-in prefix_symbols.h) so it shares one program with crd-crypto's AWS-LC and OpenSSL 4.0; linked only into crd-crypto-board for the crd-crypto-board-smoke CTest and the boards; never into an engine module or a default build. LICENSE read from the archive: Apache-2.0 for libcrypto and libssl (fiat-crypto Apache-2.0; the Go-licensed TLS test suite is not compiled). Pinned as a testing download under the user's approval of 2026-11-01 (docs/sessions/2026-11-03-net-2-crypto-boards.md).

nlohmann_json.note: nlohmann/json 3.12.0 (released 2025-04-11, the newest release on 2026-11-02), a build dependency of MLSpp only: MLSpp's CMake requires its package (find_package(nlohmann_json)), which its own CMake installs, header-only, into the MLS interop test's build tree; no Cerid unit includes it. LICENSE.MIT read from the archive: MIT, (c) 2013-2025 Niels Lohmann. Pinned as a testing download under the user's approval of 2026-11-01 (docs/sessions/2026-11-02-net-2-mls-interop-mlspp.md).

tpm2-tss.provenance: https://github.com/tpm2-software/tpm2-tss/releases/tag/4.0.1 (the tag's commit, the version of Ubuntu 24.04's tss2 libraries; its include/tss2 is byte for byte the release archive's, compared 2026-11-03)
tpm2-tss.note: The TCG TPM2 Software Stack 4.0.1: its public headers only (include/tss2: the TPM 2.0 types, ESYS, MU and the TCTI loader), which crd-crypto compiles its Linux TPM protector and device against (tpm_tss2.cpp, NET.2 decision K13); the libraries are never linked: crd-crypto loads the system's libtss2-esys.so.0, libtss2-tctildr.so.0 and libtss2-mu.so.0 at run time (the ESYS 3.0.2 ABI), so a system without them answers Unavailable. Fetched on Linux configures only. LICENSE read from the archive: BSD-2-Clause, (c) the tpm2-software contributors and Intel. Pinned as a build input under the user's approval of 2026-11-01 (docs/sessions/2026-11-03-net-2-tpm-linux.md).

pkcs11.provenance: https://docs.oasis-open.org/pkcs11/pkcs11-spec/v3.2/os/include/pkcs11-v3.2/ (the OASIS Standard of PKCS #11 3.2; the archive's published/3-02 headers are byte for byte those three files, compared 2026-11-03)
pkcs11.note: The OASIS PKCS #11 Cryptographic Token Interface 3.2 headers (published/3-02: pkcs11.h, pkcs11f.h, pkcs11t.h), from the PKCS 11 Technical Committee's repository: crd-crypto compiles its PKCS #11 key device against them (pkcs11_device.cpp, NET.2 decision K14) and calls only the 2.40 function list (C_GetFunctionList), so every module from 2.20 on answers; nothing is linked: the device loads the module its caller names at run time. Fetched on every platform. Licence: the headers' own notice, distributed under the OASIS IPR Policy (the TC's RF on RAND mode), as is. Pinned as a build input under the user's approval of 2026-11-01 (docs/sessions/2026-11-03-net-2-pkcs11-device.md).

ngtcp2.provenance: https://github.com/ngtcp2/ngtcp2/releases/tag/v1.26.0 (the tag names commit 6a22a4d7; this commit archive is the source the release packs, without the release's generated Autotools files)
ngtcp2.note: ngtcp2 1.26.0 (released 2026-11-02), an independent C implementation of QUIC and crd-net's peer (4.2a). Built by its own CMake as a separate project, libraries only (libngtcp2 and libngtcp2_crypto_ossl), against the pinned OpenSSL 4.0's QUIC TLS interface.

nghttp2.provenance: https://github.com/nghttp2/nghttp2/releases/tag/v1.71.0 (the release tarball; its SHA-256 equals the release's checksums.txt, read 2026-11-09)
nghttp2.note: nghttp2 1.71.0 (released 2026-11-02), an independent C implementation of HTTP/2 and HPACK and crd-net's HTTP/2 peer (4.2a). Built by its own CMake as a separate project, library only.

h2spec.provenance: https://github.com/summerwind/h2spec/releases/tag/v2.6.0 (the project's last release, 2020-08-04; the archive holds the one static Linux x64 binary; downloaded and hashed 2026-11-09)
h2spec.note: h2spec 2.6.0, the conformance tester for HTTP/2 implementations: run against crd-http2-peer by crd-net-http2-interop (4.2a). Test-only.

nghttp3.provenance: https://github.com/ngtcp2/nghttp3/releases/tag/v1.19.0 (the release tarball and its checksums.txt: unlike the ngtcp2 pin's commit archive it holds lib/sfparse, a git submodule a commit archive leaves empty)
nghttp3.note: nghttp3 1.19.0 (released 2026-11-02), an independent C implementation of HTTP/3 and QPACK and crd-net's HTTP/3 peer (4.2a), over the pinned ngtcp2. Built by its own CMake as a separate project, library only.

qifs.provenance: https://github.com/qpackers/qifs (its master branch's last commit; the repository has no releases)
qifs.note: The QPACK interop corpus of the IETF QUIC working group's offline interop: real header sets as QIF text and the outputs of ls-qpack, nghttp3, proxygen, quinn, f5 and qthingey at several table sizes, blocked-stream limits and acknowledgement modes (encoded/qpack-06; the wire format has not changed since), plus refused inputs (encoded/errors). crd-net's QPACK decoder must reproduce every QIF from every encoder (4.2a). Test data only, read by the crd-net-qpack-interop-qifs CTest on linux-gcc-public-checks; pinned as a testing download under the user's approval of 2026-11-01.

hpack_test_case.provenance: https://github.com/http2jp/hpack-test-case (its master branch's last commit; the repository has no releases)
hpack_test_case.note: The HPACK interop corpus of the HTTP/2 Japan community: real header stories as JSON and the blocks written by nghttp2, Go, Haskell, node-http2, python-hpack and swift-nio at the default table size, some with size changes. Read by crd-net-hpack-interop-corpus (4.2a).

mlspp.note: Cisco's MLSpp, an independent C++ implementation of RFC 9420 and the MLS peer of crd-crypto's groups (NET.2, decision M4). Its only tag is v0.1.0 (2019), so the pin is main's head on 2026-11-02 (2026-09-21). Built by its own CMake as a separate project (its library and the bytes, tls_syntax and hpke libraries it links) against the OpenSSL 4.0 pin above, so its post-quantum suites are compiled (WITH_PQ), linked only into crd-mlspp-peer for the crd-crypto-mls-interop-mlspp CTest; never into an engine module or a default build. LICENSE read from the archive: BSD-2-Clause, (c) 2018 Cisco Systems; third_party/variant.hpp BSL-1.0, (c) 2015-2017 Michael Park. Pinned as a testing download under the user's approval of 2026-11-01 (docs/sessions/2026-11-02-net-2-mls-interop-mlspp.md).

nasm.note: The NASM project's Windows x64 release build of 2.16.03 (2024-04-17; nasm.exe SHA-256 a93276636266516421cc9b422f47476c21f7a2949f1ae251556b2f1d33a3be04): AWS-LC's Windows x64 assembler, acquired at configure time on Windows x64 only, through the same verified, cached path as the source packages. wycheproof.note: Project Wycheproof's test vectors at main of 2026-10-23 (testvectors_v1: AEAD, HKDF, ECDH, ECDSA, EdDSA, ML-DSA and ML-KEM): data the crd-crypto tests read as their oracle; never compiled or shipped.

mls-vectors.note: The IETF MLS working group's test vectors at main of 2026-10-07 (test-vectors/: tree math, crypto basics, deserialization, secret tree, key schedule, message protection, transcript hashes, PSKs, Welcome, tree operations and validation, TreeKEM, messages, passive clients), cross-generated and checked by the RFC 9420 implementations: data the crd-crypto MLS tests read as their oracle; never compiled, redistributed or shipped. The repository states no licence of its own; it is a working-group repository whose contributions fall under the IETF Note Well (BCP 78 and 79), read 2026-11-02. Pinned as a testing download (pre-approved, user 2026-10-30).

Pinned as a testing download (pre-approved, user 2026-10-30).

boost.note: The Boost 1.92.0 release (the publisher's manifest names commit afdfa32505af73e3d208144b3f623f0096cb62b6, created 2026-08-05; the archive is not commit-addressed, so the commit is not a url field). hptt.note: HPTT, Paul Springer's tensor transpose (no release tag; the commit of the permute board's earlier local clone). pocketfft.note: pocketfft's C++ header (the cpp branch's head on 2026-10-31; the project tags no release), compiled only into crd-bench-pocketfft-peer, the FFT and DCT boards' peer library, without its thread pool; never into an engine module or a default build. LICENSE read from the archive: BSD-3-Clause, (c) 2011-2024 Intel Corporation. ntp.provenance: The Network Time Foundation's release of the RFC 5905 reference implementation; the SHA-256 is the one it publishes beside the tarball (read 2026-11-07)

nanorq.provenance: The head of sleepybishop/nanorq's stable branch (2026-10-25, performance fixes and tweaks #28); the project tags no releases. LICENSE read from the archive
nanorq.note: A C implementation of RFC 6330 and the first peer of hesap-net's RaptorQ code (HESAP-NET): lib/ and deps/obl compiled as crd-raptorq-peers on the complete-tier linux-gcc-public-checks lane (GCC's target attributes and cpu checks, so no MSVC lane); never in an engine module or a default build.

serialize.provenance: Glenn Fiedler's serialize, the bit stream library of yojimbo, at its release tag (read 2026-11-07)

bitsery.provenance: Mindaugas Vinkelis' bitsery, the header-only bit-packing serializer for games, at its latest release tag (read 2026-11-08)
bitsery.note: A bit-packing peer of NET.3's serializer budget board: include/ compiled by tests/foundation/net/board/peer_bitsery.cpp only; never in a shipped build.

zpp_bits.provenance: Eyal Z's zpp_bits, the C++20 byte serializer that leads the published serializer benchmarks, at its latest release tag (read 2026-11-08)
zpp_bits.note: A byte-oriented peer of NET.3's serializer budget board: zpp_bits.h compiled by tests/foundation/net/board/peer_zpp_bits.cpp only; never in a shipped build.

protozero.provenance: Mapbox's protozero, a minimal header-only codec of protobuf's wire format, at its latest release tag (read 2026-11-08)
protozero.note: The protobuf-format peer of NET.3's serializer budget board: include/ compiled by tests/foundation/net/board/peer_protozero.cpp only; never in a shipped build.

flatbuffers.provenance: Google's FlatBuffers at its release tag v25.12.19 (the plain tag; the later dated re-tag v25.12.19-2026-02-06-03fffb2 is not used), read 2026-11-08

capnproto.provenance: Cap'n Proto at its latest release tag v1.5.0 (the project tags releases without GitHub release entries), read 2026-11-08
capnproto.note: A zero-copy peer of NET.3's serializer budget board: c++/ built by its own CMake as a separate project (static kj and capnp, the capnp and capnpc-c++ compilers; no OpenSSL, zlib, fibers or tests), which generates C++ from tests/foundation/net/board/board.capnp, linked only into crd-serialize-peers through tests/foundation/net/board/peer_capnproto.cpp; never in a shipped build.

networked-physics-snapshot.provenance: Glenn Fiedler's GDC 2015 networked physics demo, the source of the smallest-three method, at the repository's last commit; one file, because the repository's assets and libraries weigh 350 MB (read 2026-11-07)
networked-physics-snapshot.note: The reference of hesap-net's smallest-three quaternions (HESAP-NET): compressed_quaternion and compressed_quaternion_64, cut verbatim from src/game/Snapshot.h at configure time and compiled by tests/numerics/hesap-net/quantize_peers.cpp on its few stand-ins; never in a shipped build.

vectorial-quat4f.provenance: Mikko Lehtonen's vectorial as the GDC 2015 networked physics demo carries it, at the commit of Snapshot.h above; one file, as that pin is (read 2026-11-07)
vectorial-quat4f.note: The reference of hesap-net's nlerp and slerp (HESAP-NET): both cut verbatim from external/vectorial/quat4f.h at configure time and compiled by tests/numerics/hesap-net/motion_peers.cpp on stand-ins with the arithmetic of vectorial's scalar backend; never in a shipped build.

kdis.provenance: Karl Jones's KDIS, a C++ implementation of IEEE 1278.1, at the head of its own repository (2026-03-02; read 2026-11-07)
kdis.note: The reference of hesap-net's IEEE 1278.1 dead reckoning (HESAP-NET): src/Extras/DeadReckoningCalculator.cpp and the data types it uses, compiled by tests/numerics/hesap-net/CMakeLists.txt as crd-dead-reckoning-peers; never in a shipped build.

openfec.provenance: INRIA's OpenFEC 1.4.2, the codec of RFC 5510's authors, through the fork that maintains it: openfec.org is a parked domain with no archive (checked 2026-11-06), and roc-streaming/openfec's tag v1.4.2.12 names this commit (2025-04-16)
openfec.note: The second reference of hesap-net's Reed-Solomon code (HESAP-NET). src/lib_stable/reed-solomon_gf_2_m with its Galois field utilities, compiled as crd-openfec-peer on the complete-tier linux-gcc-public-checks lane (it uses C variable-length arrays, so no MSVC lane); never in an engine module or a default build. highway.note: Google Highway's library (hwy, by its own CMake with tests, examples, contrib and install off), linked only into crd-bench-highway-peer, the dispatch-cost board's peer library (ADR-0134 §8); never into an engine module or a default build. LICENSE read from the archive: dual-licensed, Apache License 2.0 or the BSD 3-Clause License, at the user's choice.

tracy.note: Tracy Profiler's client (public/TracyClient.cpp), compiled only into crd-diag-overhead-tracy, the DIAG.11b peer harness (docs/bench/2026-10-26-diag-11b-tracy-peer.md); never into an engine module or a default build. LICENSE read from the archive: BSD-3-Clause, (c) 2017-2026 Bartosz Taudul. The client bundles rpmalloc (public domain), moodycamel's concurrentqueue (Simplified BSD), Erik Rigtorp's SPSCQueue (MIT), LZ4 (BSD-2-Clause) and libbacktrace (BSD-3-Clause, Free Software Foundation).

nlopt.note: NLopt, the reference oracle of hesap-opt's COBYLA, NEWUOA and BOBYQA ports (the release current when they were ported, 2026-06-10). Its library builds by its own CMake as a separate project, static, without its C++, Luksan and binding parts, linked only into cobyla_difftest, newuoa_difftest and bobyqa_difftest with each algorithm's source compiled again (tests/numerics/hesap-opt/nlopt); never into an engine module or a default build. COPYRIGHT and the three algorithms' COPYRIGHT files read from the archive: MIT, (c) 2007-2020 Massachusetts Institute of Technology and contributors; COBYLA (c) 1992 M. J. D. Powell, 2004 Jean-Sebastien Roy, 2008 Steven G. Johnson; NEWUOA (c) 2004 and BOBYQA (c) 2009 M. J. D. Powell, with MIT's modifications. The Luksan solvers (LGPL) are not built.

ggml.note: ggml, the reference implementation of the Q8_0 block format, the nn board's same-format peer (docs/bench/2026-07-05-v14m-nn.md, which ran an unversioned llama.cpp master; this is the newest ggml release on 2026-11-01). vkfft.note: VkFFT, the GPU FFT board's specialized Vulkan peer (docs/bench/2026-07-13-gpu-fft-cufft-gold.md, which built an unversioned clone; v1.3.4 is the newest release on 2026-11-01). Its header library (vkFFT/) and its benchmark utilities (benchmark_scripts/vkFFT_scripts: utils_VkFFT.cpp, the Vulkan device, fence, pool and buffer helpers) build only into bench_gpu_fft_vkfft (runtime/CMakeLists.txt) with the Vulkan backend against the host's glslang; never into an engine module or a default build. LICENSE read from the archive: MIT, (c) 2020-present Dmitrii Tolmachev. The archive's metal-cpp copy (Apache-2.0) is not used.

sde-linux.note: Intel's published SHA-256 (matched by the archive the user approved on 2026-10-27); the emulator of the avx512 kernel arms (ADR-0134 §8), installed whole by scripts/install-sde.py.

ninja-linux.note: Ninja 1.11.1, the version seanmiddleditch/gha-setup-ninja v5 installed by default before the workflow replaced that Node 20 action (2026-10-26); installed by scripts/install-ninja.py, which checks the archive, the binary and `ninja --version`. The release assets predate GitHub's recorded digests; the SHA-256 values were computed from the downloaded release files.

ninja-macos.note: The same Ninja 1.11.1 release's macOS build (universal x86_64 and arm64) for the macOS lane (NET.2 decision K16, 2026-11-04); installed by scripts/install-ninja.py like the others. The release assets predate GitHub's recorded digests; the SHA-256 values were computed from the downloaded release file (277306 bytes).

llvm.note: LLVM's Windows x64 release archive (GitHub's recorded digest matches); the hosted clang-tidy lane's strict-analysis tool, installed by scripts/install-clang-tidy.py: only bin/clang-tidy.exe and clang's builtin headers, laid out as bin/ and lib/clang/20/include. Its clang-tidy.exe is byte-identical to the developer host's C:/LLVM-20.1.8 (checked 2026-10-26). Replaced KyleMayes/install-llvm-action, which has no Node 24 release.

genmc.note: Built from source by scripts/install-genmc.py against the runner's apt LLVM of llvm_major (llvm-20-dev, clang-20; the exact package versions are recorded with dpkg-query). Parts of lli/Runtime are LLVM 3.5 derived under NCSA as well as Apache/MIT.

node-linux-x64.note: Node.js 24 LTS (Krypton, 2026-10-14), installed whole by scripts/install-node.py for the repository's npm tools, each run from a committed lockfile with every transitive SHA-512 integrity: the dashboard publisher (ci/dashboard/generate.py publish, wrangler) and the MCP Inspector of MCP-ADAPT.0's evidence (tests/tools/ceridc/mcp_inspector.py). Downloaded and hashed 2026-10-30; matches nodejs.org SHASUMS256.txt.

rust-linux-x64.note: Rust 1.99.1 (2026-10-15 stable), the compiler, standard library, Cargo and Clippy for Linux x64 from the Rust project's component archives (SHA-256 and sizes matched against the dated stable channel manifest, verified on download). scripts/install-rust.py unpacks each archive's component directory into one prefix (~/.cerid/tools/rust/<version>/linux-x64, the layout rustup installs: bin/rustc, bin/cargo, lib/rustlib/<target>), leaving the installer's script and metadata out and each archive's licences under licenses/<archive>/. It lints (cargo clippy, warnings as errors) and builds crd-openmls-peer, the OpenMLS member program of the MLS interoperability test (CRD_BUILD_MLS_VS_OPENMLS, NET.2 decision M4), whose crates are pinned by its committed Cargo.lock (tools/openmls-crates). Never an engine module or a shipped build. Pinned as a testing download under the user's approval of 2026-11-01.

gnome-keyring-linux-x64.note: Ubuntu 24.04's gnome-keyring 46.1 (noble-updates) and the GCR 3.41.2 libraries it needs beyond a stock system (libgck-1-0, libgcr-base-3-1), from Launchpad's librarian, whose files are never removed (the same bytes the Ubuntu archive serves, checked 2026-11-02). The Secret Service of the key store's Linux protector tests (NET.2 decision K10, CRD_BUILD_SECRET_SERVICE_VS_GNOME_KEYRING), unpacked by scripts/install-gnome-keyring.py with dpkg-deb -x and run in a session bus of its own; never linked or shipped. Licences from the packages' Debian copyright files: GPL-2+ (the daemon) and LGPL-2.1+ (GCK, GCR).

swtpm-linux-x64.note: Ubuntu 24.04's swtpm 0.7.3 and libtpms 0.9.3 (noble-updates), the TPM 2.0 simulator, and the tss2 4.0.1-7.1ubuntu5.1 libraries crd-crypto loads at run time (libtss2-esys, -sys, -mu, -tctildr and the swtpm TCTI) with the pcap TCTI that records the bus, from Launchpad's librarian, whose files are never removed (the same bytes the Ubuntu archive serves, checked 2026-11-03). The TPM the key store's Linux protector and device are tested against (NET.2 decision K13, CRD_BUILD_TPM_VS_SWTPM), unpacked by scripts/install-swtpm.py with dpkg-deb -x and run by tests/foundation/crypto/tpm_simulator_session.py; never linked or shipped. Licences from the packages' Debian copyright files: BSD-3-Clause (swtpm, libtpms) and BSD-2-Clause (tss2), which also list the TCG and IBM reference-code licences, CPL-1.0 and GPL-3 for parts of the sources and build scripts. Pinned as a testing download (pre-approved, user 2026-10-30).

softhsm-linux-x64.note: Ubuntu 24.04's SoftHSM 2.6.1 (softhsm2, softhsm2-common, libsofthsm2), a PKCS #11 token in software, and OpenSC 0.25.0~rc1 (noble-updates) for its pkcs11-spy.so, a PKCS #11 module that records every call it passes to another, from Launchpad's librarian, whose files are never removed (the same bytes the Ubuntu archive serves, checked 2026-11-03). The token the key store's PKCS #11 device is tested against (NET.2 decision K14, CRD_BUILD_PKCS11_VS_SOFTHSM), unpacked by scripts/install-softhsm.py with dpkg-deb -x and run by tests/foundation/crypto/pkcs11_token_session.py; never linked or shipped. Both need only the system's libcrypto.so.3 (ldd, 2026-11-03). Licences from the packages' Debian copyright files: BSD-2-Clause (SoftHSM, with BSD-4-Clause, Expat, ISC and IBM notices for parts) and LGPL-2.1+ (OpenSC). Pinned as a testing download (pre-approved, user 2026-10-30).

nasm-linux-x64.note: Ubuntu 24.04's NASM 2.16.01 (noble release pocket), from Launchpad's librarian, whose files are never removed; the SHA-256 and size are the ones Launchpad's API records for the publication (binaryFileUrls with include_meta, checked 2026-11-04). The assembler of ISA-L's x86-64 erasure code on Linux (HESAP-NET, CRD_BUILD_ERASURE_VS_ISAL: the assembly peer of the Reed-Solomon oracle and of crd-hesap-erasure-board), unpacked by scripts/install-nasm.py with dpkg-deb -x; never linked or shipped. Needs only libc (ldd, 2026-11-04). Licence from the package's Debian copyright file: BSD-2-Clause (NASM; the Debian packaging is GPL-2.0-or-later and none of it is installed as code). ISA-L 2.32.1 needs NASM 2.14.01 or later. Pinned as a testing download (pre-approved, user 2026-10-30).

tamarin-linux-x64.note: The Tamarin prover 1.12.0 (its Linux x64 release binary) and the Maude 3.5.1 rewriting engine it runs on (Maude's Linux x86_64 release zip), unpacked into one directory: the protocol model checker of NET.2's model clause (tests/foundation/crypto/model, scripts/check-protocol-model.py). Each archive's SHA-256 matched the digest GitHub publishes for the release asset on retrieval, 2026-11-03, and is recorded here; scripts/install-tamarin.py installs them into ~/.cerid/tools/tamarin/<version> and requires `tamarin-prover --version` to report both pinned versions. A testing tool only: never linked into or shipped with Cerid.

android-ndk-linux-x64.note: Android NDK r30 (Pkg.Revision 30.0.16248370, the repository index's newest channel-0 NDK on 2026-11-03), Google's Linux x64 release zip. Its size and SHA-1 were matched against the SDK repository index (provenance) on retrieval, 2026-11-03, and its SHA-256 recorded here. scripts/install-android-ndk.py unpacks the archive's android-ndk-r30/ directory into ~/.cerid/tools/android-ndk/<version> (pins.install_tree's zip reader keeps file modes and the 39 symbolic links) and checks source.properties. It builds crd-crypto's Android closure and the Keystore protector's tests (NET.2). Never an engine module or a shipped build. Pinned as a testing SDK under the user's order of 2026-11-03.

android-platform-tools-linux.note: Android SDK Platform-Tools 37.0.1 (the repository index's channel-0 release on 2026-11-03), Google's Linux zip; size and SHA-1 matched against the index (provenance) on retrieval, 2026-11-03, SHA-256 recorded here. Its adb drives the emulator for the Android test lane: scripts/install-android-emulator.py unpacks it into <sdk>/platform-tools and scripts/android-device.py runs every Android test program through it (NET.2). Never shipped. Pinned as a testing SDK under the user's order of 2026-11-03.

android-emulator-linux-x64.note: Android Emulator 37.2.13 (build 16740729, the repository index's channel-0 release on 2026-11-03), Google's Linux x64 zip; size and SHA-1 matched against the index (provenance) on retrieval, 2026-11-03, SHA-256 recorded here. scripts/install-android-emulator.py unpacks it into <sdk>/emulator and checks source.properties; scripts/android-device.py boots the pinned system image in it, headless, under KVM, for the Android test lane (NET.2). Never shipped. Pinned as a testing emulator under the user's order of 2026-11-03.

android-system-image-31-x86_64.note: The Android 12 (API 31, the Android preset's ANDROID_PLATFORM floor) default AOSP x86_64 system image, revision 5 in the system-image index (provenance; its source.properties says Pkg.Revision 3), Google's zip; size and SHA-1 matched against the index on retrieval, 2026-11-03, SHA-256 recorded here. scripts/install-android-emulator.py unpacks it into <sdk>/system-images/android-31/default/x86_64, checks its API level, ABI and tag, and writes the AVD the Android test lane boots (NET.2: crd-crypto's tests and the Keystore protector). Never shipped. Pinned as a testing emulator image under the user's order of 2026-11-03.

android-build-tools-linux.note: Android SDK Build-Tools 37.0.0 (the repository index's newest channel-0 release on 2026-11-03), Google's Linux zip; size and SHA-1 matched against the index (provenance) on retrieval, 2026-11-03, SHA-256 recorded here. scripts/install-android-emulator.py unpacks it into <sdk>/build-tools/37.0.0 and checks source.properties; scripts/android-app.py builds the Android test lane's instrumentation APK with its d8, aapt2, zipalign and apksigner (NET.2: the Keystore protector proven in an application process). Never shipped. Pinned as a testing SDK under the user's order of 2026-11-03.

android-platform-31.note: The Android 12 SDK platform (API 31, revision 1, the Android preset's ANDROID_PLATFORM and the pinned system image's level), Google's zip; size and SHA-1 matched against the index (provenance) on retrieval, 2026-11-03, SHA-256 recorded here. scripts/install-android-emulator.py unpacks it into <sdk>/platforms/android-31 and checks its API level; its android.jar is the class path the instrumentation APK compiles and links against (NET.2). Never shipped. Pinned as a testing SDK under the user's order of 2026-11-03.

temurin-jdk-21-linux-x64.note: Eclipse Temurin JDK 21.0.13+9 (the newest Temurin 21 LTS release on 2026-11-03), Adoptium's Linux x64 tarball from its GitHub release; its SHA-256 matched the release's published .sha256.txt (provenance) on retrieval, 2026-11-03. scripts/install-android-emulator.py unpacks it into <sdk>/jdk and checks the release file's JAVA_RUNTIME_VERSION; its javac, keytool and java (for d8 and apksigner) build the Android test lane's instrumentation APK (NET.2). Never shipped, never the runner image's JDK. Pinned as a testing SDK under the user's order of 2026-11-03.

raptorq-crates.note: raptorq 2.0.1 (2026-03-09) with no optional feature, a crate without dependencies: the second peer of hesap-net's RaptorQ code (CRD_BUILD_RAPTORQ_VS_PEERS, HESAP-NET), linked as a static library into crd-hesap-raptorq-peer-tests and crd-hesap-raptorq-board. The committed Cargo.lock is the pin: the crate from crates.io at the version and SHA-256 it names, which `cargo build --locked` verifies on download. Built by the pinned Rust (tools/rust-linux-x64) into the build tree (CARGO_HOME there too); linked into no engine module and never shipped. LICENSE read from the crate archive (Apache-2.0). Pinned as a testing download under the user's approval.

openmls-crates.note: OpenMLS 0.9.2 (2026-10-22, the release with GHSA-p276-g3f3-wwgh and GHSA-94v4-rg25-x625 fixed) with its RustCrypto provider and basic credentials: the crate set of crd-openmls-peer, the OpenMLS member program of the MLS interoperability test (CRD_BUILD_MLS_VS_OPENMLS, NET.2 decision M4). The committed Cargo.lock is the pin: every crate from crates.io at the version and SHA-256 it names, which `cargo build --locked` verifies on download, as npm ci does a committed package-lock (check-pins.py checks each entry names crates.io and a 64-hex checksum, and the manifest requires this version exactly). Built by the pinned Rust (tools/rust-linux-x64) into the build tree (CARGO_HOME there too); linked into no engine module and never shipped. OpenMLS is MIT (its LICENSE, read from the v0.9.2 archive, commit 8a8f83b4). The 147 crates the build compiles (of the 195 the lockfile resolves, the rest optional or for other targets) declare MIT, Apache-2.0 or either, but for BSD-3-Clause (curve25519-dalek, ed25519-dalek, x25519-dalek, subtle), MPL-2.0 (hpke-rs and its three providers), Unlicense OR MIT and Unicode-3.0 terms (read from each crate's manifest, 2026-11-02); none is redistributed, the program being test-only. Pinned as a testing download under the user's approval of 2026-11-01.

quiche-crates.note: quiche 0.30.0 (2026-09-17) with BoringSSL through the boring 5.4.0 crates, and rcgen over ring for the peer's self-signed certificate: the crate set of crd-quiche-peer, the second HTTP/3 implementation of http3_interop.py (CRD_BUILD_HTTP3_VS_QUICHE, 4.2a). The committed Cargo.lock is the pin: every crate from crates.io at the version and SHA-256 it names, which `cargo build --locked` verifies on download. Test-only, in no shipped build.

go-linux-x64.note: Go 1.27.3 (2026-10-19), installed whole by scripts/install-go.py for the repository's Go test peers (crd-webtransport-go-peer), each built from a committed go.sum with GOTOOLCHAIN=local. Downloaded and hashed 2026-11-09; the SHA-256 is the one go.dev/dl/?mode=json publishes. Test-only, in no shipped build.

webtransport-go-modules.note: webtransport-go 0.13.0 (2026-08-30) over quic-go 0.62.0 and Go's crypto/tls: the module set of crd-webtransport-go-peer, the webtransport-h3 peer of the WebTransport interoperability test (CRD_BUILD_WEBTRANSPORT_VS_GO, 4.2a). The committed go.sum is the pin: every module from proxy.golang.org at the version and h1 hash it names, which the build checks on download. Test-only, in no shipped build.

web-transport-quinn-crates.note: web-transport-quinn 0.13.6 (2026-11-03) over Quinn 0.11.12, with rustls 0.23.46 and aws-lc-rs, and rcgen for the peer's self-signed certificate: the crate set of crd-webtransport-quinn-peer, the legacy-spelling peer of the WebTransport interoperability test (CRD_BUILD_WEBTRANSPORT_VS_QUINN, 4.2a). The committed Cargo.lock is the pin: every crate from crates.io at the version and SHA-256 it names, which `cargo build --locked` verifies on download. Test-only, in no shipped build.

qmux-crates.note: qmux 0.6.6 (2026-10-23, draft-ietf-quic-qmux-02) with its TLS and WebSocket (tokio-tungstenite 0.30) transports over rustls 0.23.46 and aws-lc-rs, h2 0.4.20 (2026-10-06) for its WebSocket tunnels over HTTP/2 (RFC 8441), and rcgen for the peer's self-signed certificate: the crate set of crd-qmux-crate-peer, the second implementation of the QMux interoperability test (CRD_BUILD_QMUX_VS_CRATE, 4.2a). The committed Cargo.lock is the pin: every crate from crates.io at the version and SHA-256 it names, which `cargo build --locked` verifies on download. Test-only, in no shipped build.

cuda-linux-x64.note: The CUDA Toolkit 13.3.1 (2026-06-29), the measuring PC's toolkit, from NVIDIA's redistributable component archives for linux-x86_64 (SHA-256 and sizes from the release manifest, verified on download): the compiler (nvcc, crt headers, libNVVM), the runtime, CCCL (CUB), NVRTC, nvJitLink, cuFFT and cuBLAS/cuBLASLt. scripts/install-cuda.py unpacks them into one prefix (~/.cerid/tools/cuda/<version>; lib64 links to lib, where nvcc's profile looks for the runtime), the CUDAToolkit_ROOT of the CUDA peer programs of the GPU compute and FFT boards (CRD_BUILD_GPU_VS_CUDA, scripts/run_bench_gpu_cuda.sh) on a Linux host; a Windows host uses its installed toolkit (CUDA_PATH). Never in CI, an engine module's default build or a shipped build. Licence: the NVIDIA CUDA Toolkit EULA, a no-charge licence for use (CCCL: Apache-2.0, libcu++ with LLVM exceptions), each archive's LICENSE kept under licenses/<archive>/ of the prefix; the components are not redistributed.

bake-python-windows.note: The own-CI Windows image bake (ci/executors/gce_vm.py) installs it for all users; 3.12.10 is the last 3.12 release with a Windows installer, the series the hosted workflow's setup-python uses. Downloaded and hashed 2026-10-31; Authenticode-signed by the Python Software Foundation.

bake-git-windows.note: The own-CI Windows image bake installs it silently; the digest is GitHub's recorded asset digest, checked against the download.

bake-cmake-windows.note: The own-CI Windows image bake installs it on the system PATH; the same release as bake-cmake-linux-*. The digest is GitHub's recorded asset digest, checked against the download.

bake-cmake-linux-x64.note: The own-CI x86-64 Linux image bake unpacks it under /opt and links its binaries into /usr/local/bin. The digest is GitHub's recorded asset digest, checked against the download.

bake-cmake-linux-arm64.note: The own-CI ARM64 Linux image bake unpacks it under /opt and links its binaries into /usr/local/bin. The digest is GitHub's recorded asset digest, checked against the download.

bake-vs-buildtools-windows.license: Microsoft Visual Studio Build Tools license terms
bake-vs-buildtools-windows.note: The Visual Studio 2026 Build Tools bootstrapper that https://aka.ms/vs/18/stable/vs_buildtools.exe resolved to on 2026-10-31; Authenticode-signed by Microsoft. It installs the stable channel's current toolset at bake time; the image census records the installed version (see unpinned.note).

bake-gpu-driver-installer-windows.note: Google's NVIDIA driver installer for Compute Engine Windows machines, commit-addressed; the own-CI Windows GPU image bake runs it. The driver it downloads is the one Google publishes for the machine's GPU; the image census records the installed driver. Downloaded and hashed 2026-10-31.

webrtc-bwe-sources.note: The newest release branch of libwebrtc on 2026-11-07, file by file through Gitiles' format=TEXT: its source archives change bytes on every request (checked 2026-11-07), and the SHA-256 and size are those of the base64 text, decoded by scripts/install-webrtc-bwe.py. The goog_cc and remote_bitrate_estimator estimators with the units they use, compiled with tests/numerics/hesap-net/webrtc-shim's plumbing as crd-webrtc-bwe-peer on the complete-tier linux-gcc-public-checks lane: the bit-exact oracle and board of hesap-net's delay trend and acknowledged rate, with rtc_base's RTP to NTP estimator and timestamp aligner for its media clock pair; rtp_rtcp's FEC codec with its RFC 8627 header reader and writer and NetEq's RED splitter, as crd-webrtc-fec-peer, for its FlexFEC and RED (HESAP-NET, CRD_BUILD_ESTIMATORS_VS_WEBRTC); never in an engine module or a default build. LICENSE and PATENTS read from the tree. Pinned as a testing download (pre-approved, user 2026-10-30).

unpinned.note: OS-provided by the pinned runner image; the Linux lanes record the installed versions with dpkg-query into the lane census (llvm-20-dev, clang-20, g++-14 and libedit-dev only on the linux-clang-tsan entry, for the GenMC build; ninja-build, clang and libclang-rt-18-dev only on the linux-arm64 lanes, whose image runs no x86-64 pinned Ninja). The MSVC toolset comes from the pinned Windows image and is recorded by the evidence bundle. The own-CI images (ci/executors/gce_vm.py) take their apt packages at bake time, and their Windows image takes the Build Tools from the stable channel of the pinned bake-vs-buildtools-windows bootstrapper; each records the installed versions in its image census.
